resources.string: Sacred dietary principles for spiritual growth
Pure vegetarian principles for spiritual elevation
You are what you eat - Satvik Scan
Onion, Garlic, Potato, Ginger, Carrot, Radish, Beetroot, Sweet Potato, Suran, etc.

"Anantkaya (multi-bodied) root vegetables – uprooting them destroys the entire plant along with countless Nigod organisms associated with it. Hence Jain tradition renounces all such underground produce. (Jain Agamas – Anantkaya Principle)"
Bulbs, roots, tubers and rhizomes growing underground serve as storage organs that harbour entire colonies of micro-organisms.

"Vinegar is produced through fermentation by micro-organisms. Some Jain traditions renounce it or exercise caution. Opinions vary across different Jain sects. (Jain Tradition – Sect-wise Differences)"
A solution produced by the fermentation of alcohol into acetic acid by Acetic Acid Bacteria.

"No explicit prohibition in Jain scriptures. Its acceptability depends on the production source, as it can be derived naturally from fruits or produced via fermentation by micro-organisms. Opinions vary across different Jain sects. (Jain Tradition – Source-dependent Differences)"
Naturally found in citrus fruits like lemon, or industrially produced via fermentation using Aspergillus niger.

"No explicit prohibition in Jain scriptures. Generally made via plant-based fermentation, but its acceptance varies by sect and individual religious practice. (Jain Tradition – Sect-wise Differences)"
A flavor enhancer manufactured by bacterial fermentation of plant-based sources such as starch, sugarcane or molasses.
"Made from Tapioca/Cassava root tubers, hence classified under the Anantkaya principle. Renounced in Jain tradition. (Jain Agamas – Anantkaya Principle)"
Starch pearls extracted from the underground tuber of Cassava plant (Manihot esculenta).

"These four are described as \'Mahavigai\' in Jain tradition. Considering ahimsa (non-violence), jiv-himsa (harm to life) and religious dietary principles, their renunciation is strongly recommended. (Traditional Jain Literature – Mahavigai)"
Honey – bee-derived product; Meat – animal-derived food; Butter – dairy fat from milk; Alcohol – produced by fermentation or distillation.
"Stale food promotes rapid growth of micro-organisms, hence renounced in Jain tradition. (Traditional Jain Dietary Principles)"
Fresh paneer made from milk becomes stale over time due to rapid microbial growth and spoilage.
"Produced through fermentation, and some varieties may use animal-derived Rennet. Its source must be verified. Opinions vary across Jain sects. (Jain Tradition – Source-dependent Differences)"
A dairy product made by coagulating and aging/fermenting milk; some types use animal-derived or microbial rennet.

"Figs belong to the Udumbar category. Jain tradition renounces Udumbar fruits because they are associated with a symbiotic life cycle involving the Fig Wasp and micro-organisms. (Jain Agamas – Udumbar Fruit)"
Fig (Ficus carica) is a Syconium-type fruit whose pollination occurs through a specific Fig Wasp.
"Being Bahubiji (containing innumerable tiny seeds), poppy seeds are renounced in Jain tradition. (Traditional Jain Guidance)"
Dried and mature seeds of the opium plant (Papaver somniferum).

"As per guidance of some Jain Acharyas, Makhana grows in ponds and water bodies, and its harvesting may cause harm to aquatic life. Hence its renunciation is advised. (Traditional Jain Guidance – Some Acharyas)"
Seeds of Euryale ferox, an aquatic plant that grows in ponds, lakes and other water bodies.

"As per guidance of some Jain Acharyas, Water Chestnut grows in water bodies and its harvesting may harm aquatic organisms. Hence its renunciation is advised. (Traditional Jain Guidance – Some Acharyas)"
Water Chestnut (Trapa spp.) is an aquatic fruit that grows in water bodies, commonly known as Singhara.
"Made from underground Anantkaya rhizomes, hence renounced in Jain tradition. (Jain Agamas – Anantkaya Principle)"
Starch derived from the underground rhizome of the Arrowroot plant (Maranta arundinacea).

"No explicit prohibition in Jain scriptures. However, some Jain Acharyas advise renunciation as cocoa production and processing may involve contamination with traces of insects. (Traditional Jain Guidance – Some Acharyas)"
Food products made from Cocoa (Theobroma cacao) beans. During industrial processing, trace amounts of insect fragments may be present within regulatory limits.
"No explicit prohibition in Jain scriptures. However, some Jain Acharyas advise renouncing Maida and yeast-based fermented food items made from it. (Traditional Jain Guidance – Some Acharyas)"
Refined flour made by milling the endosperm of wheat grains.
"No explicit prohibition in Jain scriptures. However, some Jain Acharyas advise renouncing Rava during Chaturmas and Paryushan. (Traditional Jain Guidance – Some Acharyas)"
A coarsely milled product of wheat endosperm (Coarsely Milled Wheat Endosperm).

"In some Jain traditions, dry fruits are renounced from Fagan Sud Chaudas to Kartik Sud Purnima, while their use is acceptable from Kartik Sud Purnima to Fagan Sud Purnima. (Traditional Jain Guidance)"
Dried fruits and seeds of various trees, such as almonds, cashews, pistachios, walnuts, etc.
Mono & Diglycerides, Glycerol, Fatty Acids, Disodium Guanylate
"These food additives may be derived from plant or animal sources. As per Jain tradition, their source (plant vs animal) must be verified before use. (Traditional Jain Guidance)"
Industrially produced food additives that can be derived from vegetable oils, animal fats, or microbial processes.
"Generally derived from egg whites, hence renounced as per Jain dietary guidelines. (Traditional Jain Guidance)"
A natural enzyme (Enzyme) typically extracted from the white of chicken eggs.
"Being an animal-derived product produced by honeybees, it is renounced in Jain tradition. (Traditional Jain Guidance)"
Natural wax produced by honeybees (Apis spp.) in their hive combs.
"These food additives are derived from insects or animal sources, hence renounced in Jain tradition. (Traditional Jain Guidance)"
Carmine – natural dye from Cochineal insect; Gelatin – gelling agent from animal collagen; Bone Phosphate – from animal bones; Shellac – natural resin from Lac insect.
"These flavor enhancers may be derived from plant, microbial, or animal sources. As per Jain tradition, their source must be verified. (Traditional Jain Guidance)"
Flavor enhancers that can be produced via fermentation or from animal-derived sources.
Wine, Beer, Rum, Whisky, Brandy, Vodka, Gin, Food Ethanol
"All fermented or distilled alcoholic beverages are renounced in Jain tradition as they are classified under Mahavigai (major prohibited substances). (Traditional Jain Literature – Mahavigai)"
Alcoholic substances produced by fermentation and/or distillation of sugars, grains, grapes, fruits or other plant sources.
Meat, Chicken, Fish, Prawn, Crab, Pork, Beef, Mutton, Turkey, Eggs
"All animal-derived food products are renounced following the principle of Ahimsa (non-violence) in Jain tradition. (Jain Dietary Principles)"
Food products derived from animals, birds, and aquatic creatures (Animal-derived Food Products).
Meat, Chicken, Fish, Seafood, Prawn, Crab, Oyster, Pork, Beef, Mutton, Turkey, Eggs

"Bhagwan Swaminarayan, in Shikshapatri Verse 15, has instructed the complete renunciation of meat, eggs, and all animal-derived foods. This is based on the principle of Ahimsa and pure Satvik diet. (Shikshapatri – Verse 15)"
Animal-derived food products obtained from animals, birds or aquatic creatures.
Allium Family – Onion, Garlic, Leek, Shallot, Chives

"In the Swaminarayan tradition, these Allium family substances are considered Rajasic and Tamasic. They increase lust, anger, restlessness and foul odor, hence they are renounced. (Shikshapatri tradition & BAPS/Vadtal Guidance)"
Plants of the Allium family that contain high levels of organosulfur compounds (Sulfur Compounds).
Wine, Beer, Rum, Whisky, Brandy, Vodka, Gin, Spirit, Food Ethanol
"As per Shikshapatri Verses 15 and 18, all types of alcoholic beverages and intoxicating substances must be renounced. (Shikshapatri – Verses 15 & 18)"
Alcoholic products produced through fermentation or distillation.
Bhang, Ganja, Opium, Hashish & other intoxicants
"Since they contaminate the mind and senses, the Swaminarayan tradition instructs complete renunciation of all such narcotic substances. (Shikshapatri – Verse 18)"
Psychoactive / Narcotic Substances that impair neurological and cognitive functions.
Carmine, Gelatin, Bone Phosphate, Beeswax, Shellac, Lysozyme

"These food additives are derived from insects, bees, eggs or animal sources, hence not acceptable as per Swaminarayan dietary principles. (Shikshapatri principle of animal-food renunciation & traditional Swaminarayan guidance)"

Carmine – natural dye from Cochineal insect; Gelatin – gelling agent from animal collagen; Bone Phosphate – from animal bones; Beeswax – natural wax from honeybees; Shellac – natural resin from Lac insect; Lysozyme – enzyme from egg whites.
Lecithin, Mono & Diglycerides, Fatty Acids, L-Cysteine, Glycerol, etc.

"These food additives may be derived from plant, microbial or animal sources. If their source is unclear, as per Swaminarayan tradition, their source should be verified or they should be renounced as per religious guidance."
Industrially produced food additives that may be derived from vegetable oils, animal fats, eggs, feathers, hair, or microbial fermentation processes.

"In some Swaminarayan traditions, Hing is advised to be renounced as it is considered Rajasic/Tamasic. Commercial Hing may also contain wheat flour, gum or other additives. Practices vary across different Swaminarayan institutions. (Traditional Swaminarayan Guidance)"
A spice made from the milky resin (Oleogum Resin) of the Ferula plant. Commercial Hing often contains wheat flour, rice flour or gum as additives.
